title: Connections to Neuroscience
before:
Educators, are you looking to deepen your understanding of the connection between neuroscience and conceptual thinking? Look no further. Connections to Neuroscience: Supporting Student Learning through their Well-Being explores the key topics that shape this fascinating connection. Discover how emotional engagement impacts learning.

Navigating Neuroscience

Dive into the world of neural plasticity, where you'll uncover the brain's remarkable ability to adapt and rewire itself. Explore synaptic pruning, neurotransmitters, emotional engagement, and the brain hemispheres' distinctive roles in conceptual thinking. (~6 minutes)

Explore these four articles from Edutopia then complete the reflection questions:

  • Applying Insights From Neuroscience in the Classroom
  • The Neuroscience Behind Productive Struggle
  • The Neuroscience of Narrative and Memory
  • 6 Ways to Capture Students' Attention
  • Reflection Questions
Executive Function
"Over the past several years, knowledge about executive functioning (EF) and executive function skill training has become a forefront topic in education. Why? Sound executive function skills are essential for any student to excel in both the academic and social-emotional arenas." — Everyday Executive Function Strategies, p. 4

Executive Function and Metacognition (~4 minutes)

Strategies that Support Executive Function (~9 minutes)

  • Executive Function Strategies and Resources Padlet
CASEL Framework Overview

Learn about the Collaborative for Academic, Social, and Emotional Learning (CASEL) Framework. (~5 minutes)

Want to learn more about each of the CASEL 5 — self-awareness, self-management, social awareness, relationship skills, and responsible decision-making?

  • What is the CASEL Framework?
Emotional Regulation
Fisher, Frey, and Smith view "social-emotional learning as a contextualized system of habits, dispositions, knowledge, skills, procedures, and policies that inform the way we work and learn together." — The Social-Emotional Learning Playbook, p. 3

Learn about emotional regulation and strategies to support it. (~5 minutes)

Explore these resources that support emotional regulation:

  • Plutchik's Wheel of Emotions: Exploring the Emotion Wheel
  • Anger Management: 10 Tips to Tame Your Temper — Mayo Clinic
  • The SEL Playbook Chapter 3 Free Resources

notes: 1 section header — too few for a contents list.

decisions.label: Tag a document link with the format it opens
decisions.why: 2 links on this page open a file — 2 PDF — and say nothing about it, while others in the same list carry a tag because their author typed one. The format is read from the file name, so the list stops being half-labelled. No link text changes.

decisions.label: Let very uneven cards find their own height
decisions.why: 1 row pairs a short card with one holding nearly three times as much. Equal heights stretch the short one and the difference reads as a hole, so these are allowed to sit at the height of what is in them.

decisions.label: Give the cards the width their content needs
decisions.why: 1 row holds two cards of very different weight in equal halves, and cards in a row are the same height — so the short one is stretched and the difference shows as empty space. 2.7× — 371 characters beside 135. Only the column widths change.

decisions.label: Drop the dash once the link is set apart
decisions.why: 4 of those items separate the link from its description with a dash. The link is now set in the display face at a larger size with a chevron after it, so the dash marks a boundary that is already unmistakable. Only the separator is removed — no word changes.

decisions.label: Separate a link from its description
decisions.why: 4 list items open with a link and then explain it, all at the same weight — so the thing you can click is no easier to find than the sentence about it. The link becomes the item and the explanation sits under it.

decisions.label: Use this paragraph as the page description
decisions.why: It is the page’s own opening paragraph, moved into the banner rather than rewritten.
